claim_text: Reykjavík City says it suffered a cyberattack on several of its computer systems on Nov 25 and took many digital service systems offline
summary: Reykjavík City says it suffered a cyberattack on several of its computer systems on Nov 25, 2026. As soon as the attack was detected it took security measures, including temporarily disconnecting multiple digital service systems.
detail: This is the city's own description in its notice of Nov 25. A CERT-IS official interviewed by Vísir the next day also described the attack.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Reykjavík City notice, Nov 25: "Reykjavík City experienced a cyberattack on several of its computer systems today." Steps "included temporarily disconnecting multiple digital service systems."

claim_text: The city calls it a serious cyberattack and says it is working out how the attackers breached its systems and what data they may have accessed
summary: Reykjavík City calls it a serious cyberattack and says it is working to determine how the attackers breached its systems and what data they may have accessed.
detail: The city has not said what it has found so far.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Reykjavík City notice, Nov 27: "Efforts are underway to determine how the attackers breached the systems and what data they may have accessed." Nov 26 notice: "a serious cyberattack on some of the City's computer systems".

claim_text: Reykjavík City's website still says a security incident is disrupting its online services; online applications for financial assistance are unavailable
summary: At our last check, Reykjavík City's website still said a security incident was disrupting its online services and work to restore them was under way. Online applications for financial assistance were unavailable.
detail: The notice does not list which services are back and which are not.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Notice across reykjavik.is, read Nov 28, 3:25 AM ET: "A security incident is disrupting Reykjavík City's online services. Work is underway to restore services." "Online applications for financial assistance are currently unavailable."

claim_text: The city aimed to bring most digital service systems back on Nov 27 and over the weekend, and the rest as early as the start of next week
summary: Reykjavík City said on Nov 27 it aimed to bring most digital service systems back that day and over the weekend, core and essential systems first, and the rest as early as the start of the next week.
detail: Vísir reported the same notice on Nov 27.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Reykjavík City notice, Nov 27: it "aims to bring most of its digital service systems back online today and over the weekend"; "The remaining systems could be back online as early as the start of next week."

claim_text: The city is working with the security firm Syndis and Iceland's national cyber security team, CERT-IS, and is resetting all passwords and access keys in the affected systems
summary: Reykjavík City says it is working with the security firm Syndis and CERT-IS, Iceland's national cyber security team, to review its systems, and is resetting all passwords and access keys in the affected systems.
detail: A CERT-IS official told Vísir that Syndis is doing the clean-up and restoration and that CERT-IS is helping with the analysis.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Reykjavík City notice, Nov 27: staff "are working with experts from Syndis and the CERT-IS cybersecurity response team"; "This work includes resetting all passwords and access keys across the affected systems."

claim_text: In a written answer to Vísir, the city said it did not yet know whether the attackers obtained any data, including confidential data
summary: Vísir reports that in a written answer on Nov 26 Reykjavík City said it did not have exact information on which systems were closed, and that it was not known whether the attackers had obtained any data, including confidential data.
detail: The city also told Vísir it had no exact information on which systems were closed. Its own notices say only that it is working out what data the attackers may have accessed (c002).
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Vísir, Nov 27: the city's written answer said it was not known "hvort árásaraðilarnir hefðu komist yfir einhvers konar gögn, þar á meðal trúnaðargögn" (whether the attackers got any data, including confidential data).
notes: Quotes translated from Icelandic by isitahack.com

claim_text: RÚV reports, citing its own sources, that the hackers obtained passwords and got into a Reykjavík City database; the city would not confirm whether sensitive personal data was at risk
summary: RÚV reports, citing its own sources, that the hackers obtained passwords and got into a Reykjavík City database. The city's chief administrative officer would not confirm whether sensitive personal data was at risk.
detail: The city has not said this itself. Its Nov 27 notice says it is resetting all passwords and access keys (c005) and is still working out what data may have been accessed (c002).
label: Reported
why_it_supports: RÚV, Nov 26: "Samkvæmt heimildum fréttastofu komust tölvuþrjótar yfir lykilorð og inn í gagnagrunn hjá Reykjavíkurborg" (per the newsroom's sources, hackers got passwords and into a city database).
notes: Attributed by RÚV to unnamed sources. Quotes translated from Icelandic by isitahack.com

claim_text: A CERT-IS official says the attack was aimed at certain parts of the city's information infrastructure and that what the attacker did is still being analysed
summary: A CERT-IS director told Vísir the attack was aimed at certain parts of the city's information infrastructure, that what the attacker did is still being analysed, and that services were shut as a precaution.
detail: He said the services taken down, such as applications, were not ones considered essential. He also linked more serious attacks in Iceland generally to openly available AI tools; he did not say such tools were used against the city.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Vísir, Nov 26, quoting the CERT-IS director: the attack "beindist að ákveðnum upplýsingainnviðum" (was aimed at certain information infrastructure); the systems down are "niðri í varúðarskyni" (down as a precaution).
notes: Quotes translated from Icelandic by isitahack.com

claim_text: Nobody has named the attacker, no group is reported to have claimed it, and the city has not said it was ransomware
summary: Reykjavík City has not named an attacker or said whether it was ransomware or involved a ransom demand. No outlet we read reports a group claiming it. Civil protection says tracing it will take weeks or months.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The city's three notices name no attacker, group or ransomware. Vísir, Nov 27: the civil protection head says the task ahead is "að greina nákvæmlega hvaðan árásin kom" (to analyse exactly where the attack came from).
notes: Quotes translated from Icelandic by isitahack.com

claim_text: The Blue Lagoon also reported a cyberattack to CERT-IS on Nov 25; a CERT-IS official could not be sure the two attacks are related
summary: Vísir reports the Blue Lagoon reported a cyberattack to CERT-IS the same day, Nov 25. A CERT-IS director said he could not be sure the two attacks are related, though they share some similarities.
detail: Vísir mentions the attack on the web host 1984 the week before only as background. No source we read links the Reykjavík attack to 1984.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Vísir, Nov 26: the director "segist ekki geta verið fullviss um að árásin á Bláa lónið og Reykjavíkurborg tengist" (cannot be sure the attacks are related), "en þó séu einhver líkindi" (but there are some similarities).
notes: Quotes translated from Icelandic by isitahack.com

claim_text: Iceland's civil protection and CERT-IS are keeping the national alert level for cyber threats at the uncertainty level through the weekend
summary: CERT-IS and Iceland's civil protection kept the cyber threat alert at the uncertainty level on Nov 27, to stay there through the weekend unless things change, with the next assessment on Monday, Nov 30.
detail: CERT-IS says it has received many reports of probing from known malicious indicators where defences held. The assessment does not name Reykjavík City.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: CERT-IS assessment, updated Friday Nov 27: "viðbúnaðarstig vegna netógna er því áfram á óvissustigi. Að öllu óbreyttu mun það haldast þannig fram yfir helgi og verður þá næsta stöðumat gefið út fyrri part mánudags."
notes: Quote translated from Icelandic by isitahack.com: the alert level stays at the uncertainty level through the weekend; next assessment early Monday.

claim_text: Reykjavík City is the municipal government of Iceland's capital
summary: Reykjavík City is the local government of Reykjavík, Iceland's capital. It is governed by a City Council of 23 elected councillors, and its Mayor, appointed by the council, runs the city's administration.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: City Administration page: "The City Council governs the City of Reykjavík within the framework of the Local Authorities Act." It has 23 elected councilors; the Mayor "is appointed by City Council".
